extracted.intended_audience: entrepreneurs, manufacturers, and business leaders focused on production and distribution
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for building and running a manufacturing business that emphasizes product performance, minimal waste, service-before-profit, mass distribution, and sound planning/finance. Drawn from practical experience in early automobile manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutting edge (product must perform)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a single principle on which our business rests it is that the principal part of a chisel is the cutting edge. It is what a thing does--not what it is supposed to do--that matters. The cutting edge of merchandising is the point where the product touches the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate products by actual performance at the point of consumer use. Anti-pattern: elegant materials or workmanship that do not enable the product to do its job. Example: a beautifully made tool with a dull cutting edge is 'just a piece of metal.' In factory terms, ensure both people and machines on the job are capable; if either is wrong, the other cannot compensate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize waste (materials and human effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: Waste is due largely to not understanding what one does, or being careless in doing of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize manufacturing to avoid unnecessary material waste and unnecessary human labor. Measure processes to eliminate steps requiring more force or effort than necessary. Anti-patterns include processes that require extra force because of poor tooling or mismatched machine/operator capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid greed; prioritize service over extracting profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Greed is merely a species of nearsightedness. Waste and greed block the delivery of true service. I have striven toward manufacturing with a minimum of waste, both of materials and of human effort, and then toward distribution at a minimum of profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set profit margins low enough to encourage volume distribution; treat profit as the reward for good service rather than its basis. Anti-pattern: maximizing short-term margin (e.g., overpriced replacement parts) at the expense of customer satisfaction and long-term volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute maximum wage to increase buying power
rubrics_metrics.description: In the process of manufacturing I want to distribute the maximum of wage--that is, the maximum of buying power. Since also this makes for a minimum cost and we sell at a minimum profit, we can distribute a product in consonance with buying power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider wages and employee purchasing power as part of pricing and distribution strategy. Higher wages can enable broader market demand and lower per-unit costs through volume. Example: structuring margins around volume rather than extracting high margins from a few buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1: Absence of fear of the future and veneration for the past
rubrics_metrics.description: One who fears the future, who fears failure, limits his activities. Failure is only the opportunity more intelligently to begin again. What is past is useful only as it suggests ways and means for progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage experimentation and tolerate honest failure as learning. Do not let past methods unduly constrain improvement. Anti-pattern: decision paralysis from fear of failure or blind adherence to 'the way things were done.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2: Disregard of competition (do the thing best)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever does a thing best ought to be the one to do it. It is criminal to try to get business away from another man--criminal because one is then trying to lower for personal gain the condition of one's fellow man--to rule by force instead of by intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on making the best product/service rather than on undermining competitors. Compete by quality and service rather than predatory pricing or unfair tactics. Anti-pattern: win-at-all-costs strategies that degrade industry standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3: Put service before profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a profit, business cannot extend. There is nothing inherently wrong about making a profit. ... but profit must and inevitably will come as a reward for good service. It cannot be the basis--it must be the result of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate business decisions first by the service they deliver; view profit as outcome. Anti-pattern: structuring products or operations primarily to extract profit even when service suffers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4: Manufacturing is not buying low and selling high
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturing is the process of buying materials fairly and, with the smallest possible addition of cost, transforming those materials into a consumable product and giving it to the consumer. Gambling, speculating, and sharp dealing, tend only to clog this progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manufacturing by fairness in procurement and efficiency of transformation. Avoid speculation, arbitrage, or 'sharp dealing' that disconnects price from service. Anti-pattern: treating manufacturing as financial speculation rather than production of useful goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on perfecting one good idea (one idea at a time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a good idea to start with, it is better to concentrate on perfecting it than to hunt around for a new idea. One idea at a time is about as much as any one can handle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize iterative improvement of a core product/design rather than frequent pivots. Anti-pattern: chasing many new concepts simultaneously, leading to diluted effort and poor execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan thoroughly before building; distinguish planning from experimenting
rubrics_metrics.description: I draw a plan and work out every detail on the plan before starting to build. ... Many inventors fail because they do not distinguish between planning and experimenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop comprehensive designs and plans to avoid makeshifts and improperly proportioned final products. Use experiments to validate, but rely on planned design to guide production. Anti-pattern: ad-hoc construction without coherent design leading to wasted effort and poor proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor lightness and simplicity in design
rubrics_metrics.description: I was working for lightness; the foreign makers have never seemed to appreciate what light weight means. ... The present Ford car ... is simpler than the first car.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value simpler, lighter designs that reduce cost and increase utility. Evaluate designs by whether added complexity or weight provides real service benefit. Anti-pattern: adding complexity (weight, heavy components) without meaningful performance gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care for post-sale service; don't exploit customers with parts pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: There was not much concern as to what happened to the car once it had been sold. ... It was considered good business to sell parts at the highest possible price on the theory that, since the man had already bought the car, he simply had to have the part and would be willing to pay for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure business success by customer service and lifecycle support, not just initial sale. Avoid business models that depend on overcharging for inevitable repairs or parts. Anti-pattern: treating customers as 'captive' sources of spare-part revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start small and build from earnings; distrust over-financing
rubrics_metrics.description: My idea was then and still is that if a man did his work well, the price he would get for that work, the profits and all financial matters, would care for themselves and that a business ought to start small and build itself up and out of its earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor organic growth funded by operating earnings rather than heavy upfront capitalization. Anti-pattern: launching with massive capitalization primarily to enrich promoters or to mask poor management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money is worth what it produces; do not treat invested capital as a fixed charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Money is not worth a particular amount. ... The only use of money is to buy tools to work with or the product of tools. Therefore money is worth what it will help you to produce or buy and no more. ... Any return should come after it has produced, not before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not burden operations with fixed 'interest' charges detached from production capacity. Financial evaluations should reflect productive returns, not assumed 'market' interest as an operating cost. Anti-pattern: charging the business interest as if money itself earned value apart from production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid refinancing as a substitute for sound management
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of 'refinancing' was simply the game of sending good money after bad. ... In the majority of cases the need of refinancing arises from bad management, and the effect of refinancing is simply to pay the poor managers to keep up their bad management a little longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat refinancing skeptically; address root management issues rather than extending life with new capital. Anti-pattern: repeatedly refinancing failures instead of fixing operations or exiting unviable ventures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match man and machine; minimize unnecessary exertion
rubrics_metrics.description: The cutting edge of a factory is the man and the machine on the job. If the man is not right the machine cannot be; if the machine is not right the man cannot be. For any one to be required to use more force than is absolutely necessary for the job in hand is waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design work, tools, and processes so that neither worker nor machine is overburdened. Evaluate ergonomics, tooling, and machine capability to ensure efficient force application. Anti-pattern: forcing operators to compensate for poorly designed tools or processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of experts whose advice prevents action
rubrics_metrics.description: That is the way with wise people--they are so wise and practical that they always know to a dot just why something cannot be done; they always know the limitations. That is why I never employ an expert in full bloom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance expert counsel with willingness to act; avoid paralysis-by-analysis from overly cautious specialists. Anti-pattern: allowing expert skepticism to stifle practical experimentation and forward progress.
